confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on web searches of aggregated cost-of-living sites (Numbeo, world-prices.com, TravelTables, livingcost.org, whereandwhen.net). Those sites give an inexpensive meal at about 8,000 KRW (USD 4.5-7.5), cappuccino at about USD 2.70-3.40 (Numbeo about 4,900 KRW), draft beer at about USD 2.50-3.20 and a mid-range meal for two at about USD 27-30. Some of that data is from 2023, so I nudged the estimates up slightly for July 2026 and for Jeonju's tourist hanok-village prices. I could not find Jeonju-specific prices for cocktails or wine. The cocktail estimate starts from Seoul figures (Expatistan average about 12,249 KRW, Hongdae 8,000-12,000 KRW) and is adjusted down for a smaller city. For wine I found only luxury Seoul hotel prices, which are not representative, so the wine estimate is a judgment based on the local price relationship to beer and cocktails. The accommodation anchors are general-knowledge estimates for Korean guesthouses, hanok stays, motels and three-star business hotels in summer. I did not search accommodation prices or check listings. For FX, the search found an RBA rate of 0.6720 USD per AUD for 2026-11-18 at 4:00 pm. That figure came from a search summary that cited an aggregator (ozfinancehub) and said it matched the RBA page. I did not read the RBA table directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: I treated Jeonju as a mid-sized Korean regional city with heavy domestic tourism. Its prices are below Seoul's and roughly in line with Gwangju or Daejeon. Prices around the hanok village run a little higher than the city average. Where Jeonju data was missing, mainly for cocktails and wine, I used Seoul figures and adjusted them down.
